name: twitter

dimensions.name: hook_strength
dimensions.description: Does it open with something that stops the scroll? Look at their top-performing tweets AND the ecosystem's best tweets. A bold claim, surprising data, or personal announcement = high. Vague statements = low.

dimensions.name: specificity
dimensions.description: Does the tweet contain CONCRETE, VERIFIABLE details? Score 8-10 ONLY if the tweet contains at least one of: a specific number (Brier 0.21, $2.3M, 600 predictions), a named project (Zipcode, Targon, Numinous), a specific date (July 19), or a verifiable claim (testable, not opinion). Score 4-6 for general topics without specifics. Score 1-3 for vague claims ("this is exciting", "big things coming", "the future of AI"). If you remove all specific nouns and numbers and the tweet still makes sense, it scores below 4.

dimensions.name: emotional_trigger
dimensions.description: Does it make the reader feel something? Pride, outrage, curiosity, FOMO = high. Neutral information delivery = low. Also consider: is the ecosystem buzzing about this topic right now? (check recent industry pulse)

dimensions.name: reply_inducement
dimensions.description: Does it invite response? Open questions, contrarian claims, fill-in-the-blank formats = high (replies are worth 27-150x a like). 'Thoughts?' or 'Anyone else?' = low. Specific, answerable questions = high.

dimensions.name: bookmark_worthiness
dimensions.description: Is it reference-worthy? Frameworks, data points, lists, how-tos, actionable takeaways = high (bookmarks = 10-12x a like). Opinion-only or news reactions = low.

dimensions.name: structure_readability
dimensions.description: Line breaks between hook and body? Short first line? Visual pacing? (dwell time = ~10x a like). Wall of text = low.

dimensions.name: clarity_density
dimensions.description: Maximum insight per character. Every sentence carries a distinct idea. No filler, no throat-clearing. 'Stop doing X' > 'You should probably consider stopping doing X.'

dimensions.name: link_penalty_risk
dimensions.description: Does the tweet contain an EXTERNAL URL (not a quote tweet)? No link or quote tweet only = 10 (safe). External link present = 0-3 (30-94% reach reduction). 'Link in bio/reply' workaround = 7-8. Higher score = safer.

probability_guide: Link penalty risk below 5? Cap probability at 25% (links destroy reach)
extra_considerations: Author's follower count AND engagement baseline
What's currently trending and whether the tweet relates
Time of day and whether that's a high-engagement window
Time elapsed since posting (older tweets have less room to grow)
Your calibration feedback: if your track record shows you're overconfident in a range, adjust down. If underconfident, adjust up. Use your history to improve.
